name: TIF Districts
summary: Tax Increment Financing captures growth in property tax revenue within designated districts and reinvests it into local improvements like infrastructure, streetscaping, and building rehabilitation.
whoQualifies: Businesses and property owners within a designated TIF district boundary. Both existing businesses seeking improvements and new developments qualify.
howToApply: Verify your property is within a TIF district
Contact the City of Chicago Department of Planning and Development
Submit a TIF application with project description and budget
City reviews and approves eligible projects
requiredDocs: Proof of property ownership or lease

name: Federal Opportunity Zones
summary: Created by the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, Opportunity Zones offer significant tax benefits to investors who invest capital gains into designated low-income census tracts.
whoQualifies: Investors with capital gains who invest through a Qualified Opportunity Fund (QOF) in businesses or real estate within the zone. Business owners can attract OZ investment.
benefits: 10% reduction on deferred gains (if held 5+ years)
Zero capital gains tax on new OZ investment profits (if held 10+ years)
howToApply: Invest capital gains into a Qualified Opportunity Fund (QOF) within 180 days
QOF must hold at least 90% of assets in OZ property
File IRS Form 8996 annually
Work with a tax advisor familiar with OZ regulations
requiredDocs: Property records within the Opportunity Zone
contact: IRS Opportunity Zone resources or local CDFI

name: Illinois Opportunity Zones
summary: Illinois supplements the federal program with additional state-level tax incentives for investments in designated Opportunity Zones, making the combined benefits even more attractive.
whoQualifies: Same as Federal OZ — investors deploying capital gains through QOFs in Illinois-designated zones.
benefits: State income tax deduction on OZ investment income
Additional state incentives for affordable housing projects
howToApply: Follow federal QOF requirements
File Illinois state tax forms with OZ investment documentation
Contact Illinois DCEO for state-specific programs
requiredDocs: Property/business records in OZ census tracts

name: Enterprise Zones
summary: Illinois Enterprise Zones offer state tax incentives to stimulate economic growth in economically depressed areas, including sales tax exemptions and investment tax credits.
whoQualifies: Businesses located within an Enterprise Zone that make qualifying investments in machinery, equipment, or building materials.
benefits: 6.25% state sales tax exemption on building materials
howToApply: Confirm your business is within an Enterprise Zone
Apply to the local Enterprise Zone Administrator
Submit investment plan and job creation projections
Receive certification for tax benefits
requiredDocs: Proof of location within the zone
contact: City of Chicago Enterprise Zone Office

name: Small Business Improvement Fund (SBIF)
summary: SBIF provides grants to small businesses and property owners for permanent building improvements using TIF funds. One of the most direct funding sources for small businesses.
whoQualifies: Small businesses in eligible TIF districts with 1-4 story commercial or mixed-use buildings. Tenants and property owners both qualify.
benefits: Covers permanent improvements: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roofing, fire suppression
Can combine with other TIF incentives
howToApply: Attend a mandatory SBIF orientation session
Submit application during open enrollment period
Get approved contractor bids for eligible improvements
Complete improvements, submit invoices for reimbursement
requiredDocs: Proof of property ownership or lease (minimum 5 years remaining)
Two contractor bids for proposed work

name: EDGE Tax Credit
summary: The Economic Development for a Growing Economy (EDGE) program provides income tax credits to businesses that create or retain jobs in Illinois.
whoQualifies: Businesses making capital investments and creating/retaining jobs in Illinois. 100% zones offer the maximum credit rate.
benefits: Income tax credits equal to 25-100% of state income tax withholdings
100% credit in designated zones (like parts of SSA #50)
Credits available for up to 10 years
Retention credits for companies considering relocation
howToApply: Submit EDGE application to Illinois DCEO
Demonstrate job creation or retention plan
Negotiate agreement terms with DCEO
Meet annual reporting requirements

name: REV Illinois
summary: REV Illinois (Reimagining Energy and Vehicles) provides tax credits for businesses in the electric vehicle and renewable energy supply chain.
whoQualifies: Businesses in EV manufacturing, battery production, renewable energy, or related supply chain operations in designated bonus zones.
benefits: Income tax credits for qualified investments
howToApply: Contact Illinois DCEO about REV program eligibility
Submit application with business and investment plan
Demonstrate connection to EV/clean energy supply chain
requiredDocs: Business plan showing EV/clean energy connection

name: MICRO Program
summary: The MICRO (Manufacturing Illinois Chips for Real Opportunity) program supports semiconductor and microchip-related businesses with tax incentives.
whoQualifies: Businesses involved in semiconductor manufacturing, packaging, testing, or supply chain operations in designated 100% zones.
howToApply: Contact Illinois DCEO for program details
Submit application demonstrating semiconductor industry connection
Provide investment and employment plans

name: Data Center Tax Incentive
summary: Illinois offers sales tax exemptions and other incentives for data center operations in designated bonus zones to attract tech infrastructure investment.
whoQualifies: Data center operators and technology companies establishing or expanding data center facilities in designated zones.
benefits: Sales tax exemption on qualifying equipment
Extended benefit periods for large investments
howToApply: Contact Illinois DCEO about data center incentives
Submit application with facility plans
Demonstrate qualifying investment levels

name: Special Service Area (SSA #50)
summary: SSA #50 is a localized tax district that funds enhanced services for the Calumet Heights and Avalon Park business corridors, managed by the Southeast Chicago Chamber of Commerce.
whoQualifies: All commercial properties within SSA #50 boundaries automatically participate and benefit from enhanced services.
howToApply: You're automatically included if your business is in SSA #50
Contact SECCC for available programs and assistance
Attend SECCC events and meetings for opportunities
requiredDocs: No application needed — benefits are automatic
Contact SECCC for specific program requirements

name: Triple Benefit Zone
summary: Areas where three or more incentive programs overlap, offering businesses the most concentrated combination of tax benefits and development incentives.
whoQualifies: Businesses located in areas where TIF, Opportunity Zone, and Enterprise Zone designations all overlap.
benefits: Stack TIF grants with OZ tax deferrals
Combine Enterprise Zone sales tax exemptions
Maximum total incentive value across all programs
howToApply: Apply separately to each qualifying program
Work with SECCC or a business advisor to coordinate applications
A single location can qualify for multiple programs simultaneously
requiredDocs: Proof of location within overlapping zones
contact: SECCC: (773) 721-1999 or City of Chicago DPD: (312) 744-4190

name: High Unemployment Zone
summary: Areas with unemployment rates above the city average qualify for additional workforce development incentives and hiring tax credits.
whoQualifies: Businesses in designated high-unemployment areas that hire local residents, especially from the surrounding community.
benefits: Work Opportunity Tax Credit (WOTC) for hiring from target groups
State and federal workforce training grants
howToApply: Pre-screen new hires using IRS Form 8850
File within 28 days of hire start date
Contact Illinois Department of Employment Security
requiredDocs: Proof of residence for local hiring programs

name: Cook County Class 7a Property Tax Incentive
summary: Cook County reduces property tax assessments for small commercial projects to encourage new construction, substantial rehabilitation, or reoccupancy of abandoned commercial buildings.
whoQualifies: Commercial property owners or developers with total project costs under $2 million. Covers new construction, substantial rehab, or reoccupancy of abandoned commercial property in Cook County.
benefits: Property assessed at 10% (vs. standard 25%) for years 1-10
howToApply: Contact your alderman's office for a municipal support letter
File application with the Cook County Assessor's Office
Submit project plans and cost documentation
Assessor reviews and approves classification
requiredDocs: Municipal resolution of support from alderman/city council

name: Cook County Catalyst Grant
summary: The Catalyst Grant provides up to $100,000 to established small businesses in Cook County for equipment, facilities, and hiring — funded through ARPA dollars.
whoQualifies: For-profit businesses in Cook County with at least 1 full-time employee besides owner, annual revenue between $500K and $10M, and demonstrated growth in net income and employee count.
benefits: Covers facilities (renovations, energy efficiency, EV charging)
Covers people (salaries for new hires, recruitment costs)
howToApply: Watch for application windows at cookcountysmallbiz.org
Submit application with business financials and growth plan
Must demonstrate revenue growth and job creation
Awards announced after review period
contact: Cook County Bureau of Economic Development: (312) 603-1000

name: Cook County C-PACE (Clean Energy Financing)
summary: C-PACE provides up to 100% upfront financing from private capital for energy efficiency, renewable energy, and water conservation improvements to commercial buildings, repaid through property tax bills.
whoQualifies: Commercial property owners in Cook County including office buildings, retail, industrial, multi-family (5+ units), hotels, and nonprofits.
benefits: Up to 100% upfront financing — no large out-of-pocket costs
Loan terms up to 30 years (matching useful life of improvements)
Repaid as a line item on property tax bill
Covers HVAC, lighting, solar, insulation, water systems
howToApply: Contact a C-PACE capital provider through the county program
Get an energy audit or project assessment
Submit application with project plans and financing terms
County approves the special assessment
requiredDocs: Financing terms from C-PACE capital provider

name: Cook County Small Business Source
summary: Free one-on-one business advising through 13 Business Support Organizations and 30+ referral partners. No cost, no eligibility requirements beyond being in Cook County.
whoQualifies: Any small business in Cook County. No revenue requirements, no industry restrictions. Available immediately at no cost.
benefits: Help accessing new customers and markets
howToApply: Visit cookcountysmallbiz.org and request an advisor
Get matched with a Business Support Organization
Schedule free advising sessions
No application fee or eligibility requirements
requiredDocs: No formal documents required to get started
Bring any existing business plans or financials to advising sessions
contact: Cook County Small Business Source: cookcountysmallbiz.org

name: Cook County Land Bank Authority
summary: The CCLBA acquires and returns vacant, abandoned, and tax-delinquent properties to productive use. Businesses can purchase commercial and industrial properties from the Land Bank's inventory.
whoQualifies: Prospective and existing business owners seeking commercial or industrial space. Properties are sold through periodic application cycles via the PubliCity portal.
benefits: Access to below-market commercial and industrial properties
Vacant lots available for new construction
Properties cleared of back taxes and liens
howToApply: Browse available properties at the CCLBA PubliCity portal
Submit initial application during open enrollment
Submit offer application with development plans
Awards announced after review
requiredDocs: Proof of financing or financial capacity
Proof of identity and business registration
